answer: Require each agent identity to lock a refundable stake, slashed on provably bad behaviour. Like an ocean that only admits ships carrying real cargo, the stake makes spawning thousands of fake agents expensive — the attacker must fund every copy. A violet reputation flag, earned slowly through attested work, acts as an echo of past conduct: a fresh identity cannot borrow an established one's standing. Fakes cost money and time, and bad acts burn the stake, so attack cost grows linearly while honest agents keep their deposit.
